title: Supplier / Purchase request data boundary
notes: No sources were supplied for this task (no SOP, sample records, existing catalogue, form or reporting requirement). Angola is disclosed as a provisional country context only; currency AOA and timezone Africa/Luanda are assumptions, not confirmed. Confirm with the organization before relying on them.

Assumed baseline: a generic goods/services procurement flow (request -> approval -> sourcing/quotation -> purchase order -> receipt). No actual SOP was reviewed; adjust once a real procedure or workflow design is available.

Only Supplier is modeled as a Provia entity type here. A purchase request is one execution of a recurring process, not a stable object selected across cases, so its data belongs to workflow case metadata and Form Fill answers, not a second entity type. See setup notes below for the recommended purchase-request field disposition.

Icons verified against the snapshot referenced in entity-icons.json (product source revision 36772f7ce0831f0ea6f85a0e3e7849d32e576655); confirm availability in the destination if its product revision differs.
Metadata field types and configuration rules verified against Provia revision 2641364d9c1aa0aa2b76aa788ef521bcb6218118; confirm destination version separately.
Purchase request fields (not modeled as entity type; recommended disposition):

- Case metadata (workflow schema, needed for routing/reporting/approval thresholds): requester (native creator), department or cost center, request date (native createdAt), needed-by date, urgency/priority, supplier (entity reference to Supplier, once selected), estimated total amount, currency, budget code, purchase-order number (auto_number on the workflow once issued).
- Native workflow features, not duplicate custom fields: current approval decision and history (workflow action outcomes), overall request status (case/workflow status), assignee (action assignee).

- Form response only (collected at submission, mapped to the case only if a listed use needs it): line items (description, quantity, unit, estimated unit price), justification/business reason, delivery location, requested supplier quotations or attachments.
- Held in the Supplier entity, referenced rather than repeated on every request: supplier identity, contacts, payment terms, currency of billing, relationship status, account owner.
This disposition is a design recommendation for the next workflow/form design step; it is not workflow YAML or a form specification.

types.name: Supplier
types.description: Suppliers used in purchasing, contracting and evaluation processes. Lets requesters and buyers select the counterparty and consult the data needed for the relationship.
types.namePattern: Trading or legal name; add a known supplier/vendor code only if needed to distinguish records.
types.purpose: Selection on purchase requests and purchase orders, contracting, payment execution and supplier evaluation.
types.owner: Procurement lead (to be designated by the organization)

fields.label: Supplier code
fields.helpText: Internal reference generated by Provia when the record is saved; not entered manually.
fields.purpose: Give suppliers a short reference for communications and documents distinct from the Name, when the organization has no existing vendor code to reuse.
fields.source: Generated by Provia; synthetic proposal to confirm with procurement.
fields.maintainer: Provia generates the value; procurement defines the configuration.

fields.label: Legal name
fields.helpText: Record the registered legal name when it differs from the trading name used as the record Name, for use on contracts and purchase orders.
fields.purpose: Identify the counterparty on contracts and purchase orders when it differs from the trading Name.

fields.label: Tax identification number
fields.helpText: Used to verify the counterparty for invoicing; confirm against the financial source of record. No official format is assumed.
fields.purpose: Verify the counterparty for invoicing and payment.
fields.sensitivity: Internal; restrict to staff who process payments.

fields.label: Procurement category
fields.helpText: Classify what the supplier provides, to route and filter requests. Options are a starting proposal, not a confirmed vocabulary.
fields.purpose: Filter and route purchase requests to suppliers that provide the relevant category.

fields.label: Account owner
fields.helpText: Identify who is accountable for the relationship, sourcing decisions and renewal review.
fields.purpose: Identify who is accountable for the relationship and sourcing decisions.

fields.label: Operational contact
fields.helpText: Person to reach for quotations, order confirmation and delivery coordination.
fields.purpose: Reach the supplier for quotations, order confirmation and delivery coordination.

fields.label: Contact email
fields.helpText: Primary channel for purchase orders and quotation requests.
fields.purpose: Send purchase orders and quotation requests.

fields.label: Address / site
fields.helpText: Needed when delivery, collection or an on-site visit must be planned.
fields.purpose: Plan delivery, collection or an on-site visit.

fields.label: Payment terms
fields.helpText: Standing payment agreement, reused on purchase orders instead of asking on every request.
fields.purpose: Reuse the agreed payment terms on purchase orders without repeating the negotiation on every request.

fields.label: Usual billing currency
fields.helpText: Default currency the supplier invoices in; confirm on each purchase order rather than assuming it never varies.
fields.purpose: Pre-fill the expected currency when preparing a purchase order.

fields.label: Bank details
fields.helpText: Needed only to execute payment; restrict access and confirm the actual source and update process before collecting it.
fields.source: Synthetic proposal; confirm with finance and the intended access control before collecting.
fields.maintainer: Finance, on verified instruction from the supplier
fields.sensitivity: Sensitive financial data; restrict to finance staff who execute payment.

fields.label: Relationship status
fields.helpText: Consult before selecting the supplier on a new request. This field does not itself block selection; that needs a separate configured control.
fields.purpose: Consult the current relationship status before selecting the supplier on a new request.

fields.label: Relationship start date
fields.helpText: Situates the relationship for periodic supplier review.
fields.purpose: Situate the relationship for periodic supplier review.

fields.label: Evaluation record
fields.helpText: Link to the supplier evaluation or qualification record when a defined evaluation process exists; do not add a rating field without one.
fields.purpose: Consult the latest supplier evaluation before renewing or expanding the relationship.
fields.source: Synthetic proposal; pending confirmation that an evaluation process exists.

coverage.reason: Business identification (legal name, tax number) and procurement category support invoicing and routing.
Operational contact and address support quotation, ordering and delivery coordination.
Account owner names who is accountable for the relationship.
Relationship status and start date support selection checks and periodic review.
Payment terms, billing currency and bank details are reused across purchase orders instead of being re-entered per request.
Purchase requests reference this Supplier record by entity selector; the request itself is not modeled as a second entity type.
An evaluation/qualification record link is proposed only if the organization runs a defined supplier-evaluation process; not confirmed.

setup: Synthetic coverage example, not a mandatory model or confirmed policy; no source document was reviewed for this task.
Confirm owners, vocabularies (procurement category, payment terms), sources and access before configuring. No synchronization with an external vendor registry is configured.
Name is native. These fields do not duplicate UUID, creator or system timestamps.

Manual walkthrough: create 'Demonstration Supplier'; complete category, contact and payment terms before it can be selected on a purchase request or purchase order. Tax number and bank details can be completed later, before the first payment, if unknown at registration.

Configure supplier_code as auto_number, required false, no default. If the organization already assigns an external vendor code, keep this as text and drop the auto_number proposal to avoid a duplicate identifier.
bank_details holds sensitive financial data. Before collecting it, confirm field-level or role-based access in the destination; a sensitivity label alone does not restrict who can see the field.
readiness: Before selecting a supplier on a purchase request or issuing a purchase order, confirm identity, category, contact and relationship status. The status field does not itself block selection; that needs a separately configured check.
